memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then say to the Lord your God: 'I have removed from my house the sacred portion and have given it to the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow, according to all you commanded. I have not turned aside from your commands nor have I forgotten any of them.'" — Deut 26:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After giving the special tithe, the Israelite could stand before God and honestly say, "I have done what You commanded. I have not forgotten." This was not proud boasting; it was a clear conscience. He had obeyed, and he could say so before the God who sees everything.

There is real peace in obedience. When we know we have done what God asked — cared for the needy, kept our word, followed His ways — we can stand before Him without a nagging, guilty heart. Sin hides and makes excuses; obedience can speak openly to God.

But we must be careful here. This man's clear conscience came from actual obedience, not from pretending. He could not lie to God. And none of us obey perfectly. This is exactly why we need Christ. Our clearest conscience comes not from our own record but from His blood, which cleanses us and lets us draw near to God with confidence (Heb 10:22).

So let this verse do two things. Let it call you to real, wholehearted obedience — the kind you could honestly speak of before God. And let it drive you to Christ, whose finished work gives you a clear conscience even when your obedience falls short.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there any area where I am hiding from God rather than obeying Him?
2. Where does my confidence before God truly rest — my record, or Christ's?
3. How does obedience bring peace to my conscience?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I long to walk in honest obedience before You, with nothing hidden. Thank You that when I fall short, the blood of Christ gives me a clear conscience. Draw me near. Amen.
